subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a cautious explorer in the Underdark, wary of strange creatures and inclined to observe details, having been trained by monks to mask his emotions.
source_quote: Zalthir masks his feelings well. The monks taught him how to do that, and he was very good at it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic survivor of the Underdark, shaped by trauma and distrust, who assumes every encountered creature intends to kill him unless proven otherwise.
source_quote: Everybody we come across here in the Underdark has tried to kill us, so we are wary.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an orc who is emotionally resilient to trauma and operates with practicality, having seen worse horrors than those revealed by the Flumph.
source_quote: The trauma dumping seems to affect Thorin, but Grygum is an orc, and a practical creature, and quite frankly, he’s seen worse.

subject: The Flumph
fact: The Flumph is a psychic energy-feeder from the Underdark that relieves itself by trauma-dumping painful memories into the minds of others, and identifies as non-parasitic, non-evil, and distinct from Mind Flayers.
source_quote: I am a flumph. And my kind feeds on the psychic energy of creatures. We aren’t parasitic like the Mind Flayers; we feed on the residual background energies.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: The Cult of Demogorgon is an evil organization led by Plinki, who seeks to corrupt a mysterious egg into a dual-headed dragon to present as a mount to his dark master.
source_quote: Plinki has recently converted to the Cult of Demogorgon and wishes to turn the egg into a dual-headed dragon that he can give to his master to ride!

subject: Council of Savants and the Gray Ghosts
fact: A scholarly and secretive faction whose former members once coexisted peacefully with Duergar in the Underdark, now represented by a Derro carrying their insignia in a corrupted cave complex.
source_quote: Through the side passageway, he sees a chamber with a derro that carries the insignia of office of the Council of Savants and the Gray Ghosts.

subject: Empty Scabbard Killers
fact: A violent faction now engaged in war against the Cult of Demogorgon in the former peaceful mesa (Area 5), likely remnants of a once-harmonious community turned hostile.
source_quote: The mesa (Area 5) was once a place where folks got together to get drunk and party, but now it was a war zone between the forces of the cult of Demogorgon and the empty scabbard killers.

subject: Myconids
fact: Myconids are sentient fungal beings in the Underdark, capable of silent movement and communal behavior, with sprouts being their juvenile forms.
source_quote: These are myconids. And those little ones are sprouts, like stool.

subject: Quagoths
fact: Quagoths are monstrous, amphibious creatures of the Underdark, possibly once peaceful but now associated with madness and corruption, exemplified by Prince Derendil, a polymorphed elf.
source_quote: Behind the myconids are two spore servants; from their looks, they are quagoths. For a moment, he remembers Prince Derendil, the mad quagoth, who was a polymorphed elf.

subject: Flumph
fact: A flumph is a gelatinous, floating creature with eye-tentacles that emits a ‘flumph’ sound, feeds on residual psychic energy, and communicates telepathically with a pleasant voice.
source_quote: The creature looks like a mushroom cap with two tentacles that have eye sockets at their end. And below the mushroom cap are tentacles that float. The creature vents gases, making a “flumph” sound.

subject: Cave with the Obelisk
fact: A dangerous underground chamber containing a powerful obelisk being manipulated by Plinki to create a dual-headed dragon, accessible via a main entrance and a side passageway.
source_quote: There you saw it! A chamber with a circular pathway and a pyramid. The one known as Plinki has found this mighty and tasty obelisk and has been trying to make it do something evil.

subject: Mesa (Area 5)
fact: Once a peaceful gathering place for Derro and Duergar to party and socialize, now a war zone between the Cult of Demogorgon and the Empty Scabbard Killers after the Faerzress altered.
source_quote: The mesa (Area 5) was once a place where folks got together to get drunk and party, but now it was a war zone between the forces of the cult of Demogorgon and the empty scabbard killers.

subject: Underdark Fungi Forest
fact: A surreal, eerie forest of giant fungi and myconids, where the environment itself seems affected by the madness of the Underdark.
source_quote: And so he continues through the eerie fungi forest, following Droki’s trail.

subject: Faerzress Fluctuation
fact: The magical light of the Faerzress blinked off, then on brightly, then off again, then returned to normal — triggering widespread fear, societal collapse, and the transformation of the Underdark from a place of peace to one of violence and conspiracy.
source_quote: Some months ago, the permanent twilight of the Faerzress stopped, and the cave complex became dark. Everyone was afraid, and the Faerzress blinked on brightly and then was off. And then it blinked once more, and then it returned to its usual color.

subject: Trauma Dump
fact: The Flumph discharged stored traumatic memories into Zalthir’s mind, revealing the corruption of the Obelisk, the rise of the Cult of Demogorgon, and the fall of the Underdark’s former harmony.
source_quote: I let out all the unpleasant memories inside and into the heroes' minds, and now I feel better!

subject: The Egg and the Obelisk
fact: A mysterious egg, marked with strange symbols, is being corrupted by Plinki into a dual-headed dragon via an obelisk — a potential weapon or ritual object of immense power.
source_quote: What are the strange markings on the egg? Plinki has recently converted to the Cult of Demogorgon and wishes to turn the egg into a dual-headed dragon...

subject: The Derro Councilor
fact: A Derro bearing the insignia of the Council of Savants and the Gray Ghosts is present in the side passageway — suggesting a deeper, possibly betrayed, connection between scholarly factions and the current evil.
source_quote: Through the side passageway, he sees a chamber with a derro that carries the insignia of office of the Council of Savants and the Gray Ghosts.

subject: The Flumph’s Origin
fact: The Flumph’s knowledge of the Underdark’s history and its trauma-dumping behavior suggest it may have once lived among the peaceful communities now destroyed — raising questions about its past and true motives.
source_quote: The caves were once a hippy place, where Derro and Duergar would come to chill out, party, and be friends.

subject: 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: The day on which the Flumph revealed the corruption of the Obelisk, the fall of the Underdark’s peace, and the rise of the Cult of Demogorgon, marking a turning point in the party’s journey.
source_quote: 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut, committed to the principle that dragons have free will and that scale pigmentation does not determine personality. He believes the notion that chromatic dragons are evil is the greatest evil. He is determined to save the egg, even at great personal risk.
source_quote: Bahamut commands that I save the egg.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a pragmatic individual who seeks magical equipment and has no interest in grand missions. He initially dismisses saving the duergar Werz or defeating a cult of Demogorgon as irrelevant to his goals, but is willing to engage when prompted by evidence or logic.
source_quote: Saving the Duergar from a mad king and defeating another cult of Demogorgon is not what I am here for.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a thoughtful magician and long-time student of magic who practices daily journaling inspired by Milo Goodbarrel. He analyzes factional motivations and strategic opportunities with precision, and has deduced a profitable path forward involving evidence-based persuasion rather than direct confrontation.
source_quote: The path forward was clear, and indeed, it was very profitable.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a hardened warrior who distrusts frontal assaults and prefers stealth or unconventional escapes. He favors fleeing on the back of Thermbachaud and is skeptical of the value of gathering evidence unless it avoids war.
source_quote: We don’t have the resources to mount a full frontal assault. So we could just return, give the information, and then boogie out of here.

subject: Flumph
fact: The Flumph is a psychic energy feeder who experiences trauma dumps as emotional release. It has knowledge of hidden factions — including the Council of Savants, Grey Ghosts, assassins, and mind flayers — but cannot read minds directly. It feeds on psychic energy and is emotionally bonded to the memory of its deceased friend Buppido.
source_quote: Ever since my friend Buppido went stark raving mad…

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants was once a benevolent group but became corrupted after the blink. They are now working with Plinki to summon Demogorgon or turn him into a two-headed dragon mount. They are psychics who emit psychic energy, which the Flumph feeds on. They are the primary enemy of the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: After the blink, they became crazy. And now they are working with Plinki to try to summon Demogorgon or make him a two-headed dragon mount!

subject: Grey Ghosts
fact: The Grey Ghosts are an elusive organization suspected of engaging in evil activities. Evidence of their actions has been found, but it is not yet physical. They are believed to be connected to the city’s growing madness and are a target of Errde’s investigation.
source_quote: We found evidence of the Grey Ghosts doing something evil.

subject: Assassin’s Guild
fact: The Assassin’s Guild operates in the shadows and has targeted key figures, including the duergar Werz, using magical light blades. Their involvement is known through secondhand testimony, but physical proof is lacking. They are also suspected of working with the Council of Savants.
source_quote: The assassins are also there. The ones you said had a magical light blade that tried to kill that duergar Werz.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn leads the Keepers of the Flame, a secretive order engaged in a hidden war with the Council of Savants. Their primary objective is to secure the egg as insurance against Themberchaud. They seek exposure of the Council’s corruption and consider them their worst enemies.
source_quote: The egg is their insurance policy against Themberchaud.

subject: Stone Guards (Errde)
fact: Errde, leader of the Stone Guards, publicly believes the Council of Savants and Grey Ghosts are responsible for the city’s madness. She secretly avoids acknowledging that assassins have targeted her clan. She demands physical evidence of the Council’s corruption and proof of the Empty Scabbard Killers’ involvement.
source_quote: She wants proof of the Council of Savants' involvement with the corruption in the city. She also wants any actual evidence about the Empty Scabbard Killers.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud, the red dragon, is insecure about his authority and suspects the Keepers of the Flame have plans against him. He desires intelligence on the inner workings of the Council of Savants and the egg’s significance, though he does not directly engage with the party.
source_quote: He’s not sure that he’s in charge. And he wants information about what’s going on.

subject: the egg
fact: The egg is a powerful artifact of immense strategic value. It serves as insurance for the Keepers of the Flame against Themberchaud. Grygum, as a cleric of Bahamut, believes it must be saved, though its nature and origin remain unexplained.
source_quote: As a cleric of Bahamut, I must save the egg.

subject: psychic energy
fact: Psychic energy is emitted by psychics such as the Council of Savants and mind flayers. The Flumph feeds on this energy, which causes it to experience trauma dumps. This energy is the key to its knowledge, but not its direct perception.
source_quote: They are psychics, and they use psychic energy, and I feed on it.

subject: mind flayer
fact: A mind flayer is a psychic predator that releases powerful energy detectable by the Flumph. It is known to reside down a hallway and has been indirectly observed through the Flumph’s trauma dumps. It is dangerous and connected to the broader conspiracy.
source_quote: The Flumph had found a tasty snack in the psychic energy released by a mind flayer.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is a primordial demon lord sought to be summoned by the Council of Savants and Plinki. They aim to turn it into a two-headed dragon mount, indicating a blasphemous fusion of psionics and demonic power.
source_quote: They are working with Plinki to try to summon Demogorgon or make him a two-headed dragon mount!

subject: Whorlstone Caves
fact: The Whorlstone Caves are a contested location where key factions hide. Gartokkar and Errde cannot enter without triggering war — Gartokkar because it would reveal his power’s fragility, and Errde because it would expose her incompetence as city guardian.
source_quote: Gartokkar and Errde can’t get into the Whorlstone Caves without triggering a war.

subject: Derro hovels
fact: The Derro hovels are a place recently departed from, marking the transition back into the city of blades. Their atmosphere is oppressive and tied to the broader decay of the city.
source_quote: As we leave the Derro hovels and re-enter the city of blades...

subject: seedy bar
fact: The seedy bar is where the rest of the crew is currently holed up. It serves as their base of operations and potential recruitment point for weapons from Errde.
source_quote: We have the rest of the crew holed up in a seedy bar.

subject: obelisk room
fact: The obelisk room contains papers with critical information, but the Flumph cannot recall their contents. Their text is a potential source of physical evidence, but remains inaccessible.
source_quote: What was written on the papers in the obelisk room? ... No.

subject: physical evidence gap
fact: The party possesses testimonial knowledge about the Council of Savants, Grey Ghosts, assassins, and the egg — but lacks physical proof. Daz has determined that without tangible evidence, factions like Errde and Gartokkar will not act.
source_quote: Without physical evidence, the word of a Flumph won’t be taken seriously.

subject: strategy for persuasion
fact: Daz has deduced that the path forward lies not in combat or direct confrontation, but in leveraging existing factional rivalries and presenting verifiable, contextual evidence — such as the Flumph’s trauma-dumped knowledge — to convince Errde and Gartokkar to act.
source_quote: The path forward was clear, and indeed, it was very profitable.

subject: Thermbachaud escape plan
fact: Thorin advocates escaping on the back of Thermbachaud as an alternative to confronting factions or gathering evidence. This plan remains unconfirmed but represents a high-risk, high-reward option.
source_quote: I still like the plan of escaping on the back of Thermbachaud.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during a session of play following the party’s departure from the Derro hovels and re-entry into the city of blades. The timeline is fluid but anchored by Daz’s journaling practice and the sequence of factional revelations.
source_quote: As we leave the Derro hovels and re-enter the city of blades...

subject: trauma dump
fact: A trauma dump is an emotional release experienced by the Flumph after absorbing psychic energy. Each dump reveals fragmented knowledge about factions, locations, and threats. Multiple dumps are now required to build sufficient narrative weight for persuasion.
source_quote: Flumph, I’ll need you to trauma dump on someone. ... Make that two trauma dumps.

subject: blink
fact: The blink is a pivotal, unexplained event that caused the Council of Savants to transform from benevolent to corrupt. It is referenced as the origin of their current madness and their alliance with Plinki.
source_quote: After the blink, they became crazy.

subject: Buppido’s madness
fact: Buppido, the Flumph’s friend, went stark raving mad — an event that deeply affected the Flumph and may be linked to the increased psychic energy in the region. This trauma underpins the Flumph’s emotional state and its knowledge.
source_quote: Ever since my friend Buppido went stark raving mad…

subject: empty scabbard killings
fact: The Empty Scabbard Killers are assassins whose identities and motives are unknown. Errde seeks physical evidence of their involvement, but none has been presented yet.
source_quote: She also wants any actual evidence about the Empty Scabbard Killers.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum led the party to the Keeper of the Flame and initiated the request for assistance.
source_quote: Grygum — “We need some help.”

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is a mercantile and vengeful figure who demands proof of demonic worship and seeks to eliminate the Derro, but is open to payment for services.
source_quote:
Gartokkar — “You had some helpers, use them.”
Gartokkar — “I could give them badges!”
Gartokkar — “Compensation? COMPENSATION.”
Gartokkar — “I want proof of the involvement in demonic worship. Bring me the statue of Demogorgon.”
Gartokkar — “2000.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin challenged Gartokkar's refusal to employ helpers and later entered negotiations for payment and confidentiality.
source_quote: Thorin — “You are not employing them.”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir proposed that compensation be required for the task.
source_quote: Zalthir — “I think we need some compensation.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz smiles and shifts focus to negotiating with Errde after the transaction with Gartokkar.
source_quote: Daz smiles, “Time to talk to Errde and negotiate terms with her.”

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are slyly aware of Gartokkar’s mercantile nature and are complicit in his genocidal scheme against the Derro.
source_quote: The duergar smiled slyly when he realized we were as mercantile as he was.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are the intended target of Gartokkar’s genocidal campaign, framed as a purge of a scourge from the city.
source_quote: He was planning to engage in a genocidal war against the Derro.

subject: negotiation for payment
fact: Thorin and Gartokkar negotiated an upfront payment of 30% of 2000 gold and a confidentiality rider worth 1000 gold; an attempt to raise the upfront to half of 3000 failed.
source_quote: First, we secured an upfront payment of 30% of the 2000 gold. Then we secured a confidentiality rider worth another 1000 gold. We attempted to raise the upfront fee to half of the 3000, but Gartokkar was not biting.

subject: statue of Demogorgon
fact: The statue of Demogorgon is the demanded proof of demonic worship, to be used as leverage against the Derro.
source_quote: Bring me the statue of Demogorgon.

subject: 2000 gold
fact: The agreed-upon payment for the task is 2000 gold, with additional terms negotiated on top.
source_quote: Gartokkar — “2000.”

subject: genocidal campaign against the Derro
fact: Gartokkar plans to use proof of theft and demonic worship to convince the Deepking to eliminate the Derro, initiating a genocidal war.
source_quote: He intended to use the proof of the theft and the proof of the demonic worship to convince the Deepking that it was time to eliminate the scourge of the Derro from the city.

subject: negotiation with Errde
fact: Daz has initiated a new negotiation thread with Errde following the Gartokkar deal.
source_quote: Daz smiles, “Time to talk to Errde and negotiate terms with her.”

subject: Gartokkar's threat
fact: Gartokkar threatens violent retribution against betrayal, implying supernatural tracking ability in dark places.
source_quote: If you betray me, there is no cave, no pool of still water, no river, no place in the dark that I will not find you and hunt you down.

subject: session anchor
fact: The events described occur within a single narrative session, with no explicit temporal marker beyond sequence.
source_quote: It was then that Thorin and I entered the negotiations.
